cf.title: Proposal: JSON5 support in the JSON parsers

input.subject: Proposal: JSON5 support in the JSON parsers

verdict_reasoning: The proposal fails at level 1b on demand. The only named consumer is the author's configuration format prototype, and the thread does not say if that proposal still needs this work (demand-1, already-exists-2). An extension can build the json5 type once the parser flag exists (already-exists-1). These are answerable, but the thread has only the author's two messages, so the verdict rests on absence of evidence.

brief.title: JSON5 syntax in the JSON parser and a new json5 data type
brief.problem: Plain JSON is hard to write by hand, which the author met while prototyping a JSON-based configuration file format. The author wants JSON5 input available to SQL users and to extension authors through the common JSON parser.
brief.proposed_design: A json5 flag on JsonLexContext makes the recursive-descent parser in src/common accept the JSON5 grammar, added one feature per commit; the incremental parser stays strict-JSON only. A new json5 type stores validated input verbatim and has casts to and from json and jsonb.
user_visible_surface: New SQL data type json5, stored verbatim like json, with no functions or operators of its own.
Casts: json5 to json and jsonb (assignment, normalizing, error on Infinity/NaN); json to json5 (implicit, binary coercible); jsonb to json5 via I/O.
to_json, json_build_object, jsonb_agg and similar embed json5 values as JSON instead of as strings.
C API: new json5 parameter on makeJsonLexContextCstringLen and a json5 flag on JsonLexContext; all existing callers pass false.
libpq now links unicode_category, about 70 KB larger.
author_claims: JSON5 support helps both SQL users and extension authors, apart from the configuration format proposal.
v2 passes the full official json5-tests suite and was fuzzed against the json5 reference implementation.
The strict JSON path shows only about 1% noise in release-build benchmarks.
Changing a json column to json5 needs no table rewrite.
The first commit, comments only (JSONC), is useful by itself, and the type commit can be dropped.
brief.thread_state: Only the author has posted; v2 drops incremental parser support after a comment from Andrew in another thread. Tristan Partin is listed as reviewer but has not posted in this thread.
unclear: The thread shows no user demand for a json5 SQL type beyond the configuration format prototype.
The proposal does not say whether the configuration format proposal still depends on this work.
The proposal does not say if the implicit json to json5 cast can make function or operator resolution ambiguous.
The proposal does not say why a separate type is better than a parsing function or input option on json/jsonb.
The proposal does not say if frontend tools such as parse_manifest or OAuth code would ever use json5, given the libpq size cost.

objections.title: No user demand shown for a json5 SQL type
objections.failure_scenario: The project adds json5 as a core type with permanent catalog entries and casts, but few users store JSON5 in tables. The type cannot be removed later without breaking dumps and upgrades. Maintainers then carry an ECMAScript 5.1 grammar in the backend for a small group.
objections.argument: The only use case in message #1 is the author's configuration format prototype, and message #2 adds no users. Nobody else has posted, and the listed reviewer has not either. The thread names no -general or -bugs requests and no other databases with a JSON5 column type. A committer would likely ask, as in [P1], why a niche syntax cannot first live in an extension and prove its demand there.
objections.author_must_show: Which users or applications store hand-written JSON5 in Postgres today, and what do they do now, for example strip comments in the client before insert?

critic.reasoning: Only the author has posted, and the one use case is the author's own prototype. P1 is about a niche function, so it is weak support, but the objection stands without it.

objections.title: Clients can turn JSON5 into JSON before it reaches the server
objections.failure_scenario: An application that keeps hand-written JSON5 files converts them to JSON with a JSON5 library on the client and inserts the result into json or jsonb. That path works today on every supported release. The in-core grammar adds lexer paths in src/common and about 70 KB to libpq, and no frontend caller is shown to use them.
objections.argument: The only consumer named in message #1 is the configuration format prototype, and the thread does not say whether that proposal still depends on this work. JSON5 parsers already exist outside Postgres, and message #2 tests against the reference one. Extension authors who want JSON5 can bundle such a parser. Core placement is mainly a convenience unless a core caller, such as a server configuration file, needs it.
objections.author_must_show: Which in-core caller, backend or frontend, needs to parse JSON5 and cannot convert the input to JSON first?

critic.reasoning: The thread names one consumer, the configuration format prototype, and does not say if it still depends on this work. No in-core caller sets the json5 flag except the new type.

objections.title: The json5 type can be built as an extension on today's hooks
objections.failure_scenario: Core ships json5 as a built-in type with no functions or operators. Users who store configuration in it must cast to json or jsonb in every query. The project then keeps the type OID, the casts and the docs through every release and pg_upgrade, even if the configuration format proposal goes another way.
objections.argument: Patch 0007 adds an input function, verbatim storage, a binary-coercible cast from json, and normalizing casts to json and jsonb. An extension can already do all of this with create type, create cast ... without function and create cast with a function. For types outside the built-in OID range, to_json and json_build_object already use a cast to json if one exists. Message #1 says the type commit can be dropped, so the core need left is the parser flag.
objections.author_must_show: What does a built-in json5 type give users that an extension type, using the patched parser and the existing cast-to-json lookup, cannot?

critic.reasoning: An extension can create the type, the binary-coercible cast and the normalizing casts, and the JSON builders already use a cast to json for non-built-in types. P1 concerns a different function and must not be used as support.

other_surviving.title: A new data type where a parsing function or input option would do
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user stores configuration in a json5 column, then finds that no JSON function or operator works on it without a cast. The type now has a permanent OID, a pg_dump surface and driver mappings. If the project later adds a lax-parsing option to the standard JSON constructors, Postgres carries two ways to do one job.
other_surviving.argument: The json5 type has no functions or operators of its own, so it acts only as an input format with storage. Postgres already declares input formats in the SQL/JSON constructors and casts, and a function such as json5_to_jsonb(text) would cover the parsing need without a new type name. Message #1 says the type commit can be dropped or done differently, but neither message explains why a type is better than a function or option.
other_surviving.author_must_show: What can a user do with a json5 column that a json5-parsing function returning json or jsonb cannot do?

critic.reasoning: The docs hunk says json5 has no functions or operators, and neither message compares a type with a parsing function. The author's offer to drop the type commit does not answer the question.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Input validity depends on database encoding, which breaks dump and restore
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user stores '{café: 1}', or a value with U+00A0 whitespace, in a json5 column of a UTF8 database. They restore the dump into a LATIN1 database, where both characters exist. COPY rejects the row during restore, and the user finds out only when the restore fails.
other_surviving.argument: The documentation hunk in v2-0008 says non-ASCII whitespace and non-ASCII characters in unquoted keys are recognized only when the database encoding is UTF8. So the same text is valid json5 in one database and invalid in another, even when every character converts cleanly. The json and jsonb types do not depend on encoding in this way.
other_surviving.author_must_show: How does a json5 value accepted in a UTF8 database restore into a database with another server encoding that can represent all its characters?

critic.reasoning: The docs hunk confirms that raw non-ASCII keys and whitespace are accepted only in UTF8, so the restore failure can happen. jsonb has a similar dependence for \u escapes, so the claim that json and jsonb have none is too strong.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Every libpq user pays about 70 KB for an unused feature
other_surviving.failure_scenario: Packagers and embedded users ship a libpq about 70 KB larger. No libpq code path enables json5, since the OAuth callers pass false. The size cost falls on every client, while only backend json5 users gain.
other_surviving.argument: Message #2 says unicode_category now links into libpq for json5 whitespace and identifier rules. The commit message for 0001 shows that fe-auth-oauth.c and oauth-curl.c pass false, so libpq never takes the json5 path. The author offers to skip this part, but then the frontend and backend copies of src/common accept different JSON5 grammars.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Which frontend caller would enable json5, and if none, can the json5 code stay out of the libpq build?

critic.reasoning: Message #2 confirms the 70 KB cost, and the 0001 commit message shows all libpq callers pass false. The author's offer to skip it would leave frontend and backend accepting different grammars, so the question stays open.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Stored json5 values can fail later in casts and JSON builders
refuted.failure_scenario: An application inserts '{limit: Infinity}' into a json5 column, and the insert succeeds. A report later runs json_agg over the table, or casts the column to jsonb, and the whole query fails on that one row. The user finds out at query time, long after the data went in.
refuted.argument: Per the v2-0007 commit message and docs, json5 to json and jsonb raise an error on Infinity and NaN, and to_json and jsonb_agg use the same conversion. So the type accepts values that its only consumers reject. The column is meant to be used through json and jsonb, yet no option is described to reject such values at input.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should json5 input accept Infinity and NaN, when every cast and JSON builder that uses the value then rejects them?

critic.reasoning: Infinity and NaN are part of JSON5, and the docs hunk documents the cast error. The json type already accepts \u0000, which the cast to jsonb rejects, so this copies existing practice.

refuted.title: Validity of stored json5 values depends on database encoding and Unicode tables
refuted.failure_scenario: A user stores json5 with a U+00A0 space or a non-ASCII unquoted key in a UTF8 database. Restoring that dump into a LATIN1 database, or replicating it to a LATIN1 subscriber, sends the value through json5_in, which rejects it. The restore aborts, or the apply worker stops, only when that row arrives.
refuted.argument: The docs hunk in 0008 says non-ASCII whitespace and key characters are recognized only when the database encoding is UTF8. So the same stored text is valid in one database and invalid in another. The json type does not reject raw non-ASCII text by encoding at input. Key rules use Unicode general categories through unicode_category, so a category change in a later Unicode update could also make dump/restore across major versions fail, while pg_upgrade copies the value without checking it.
refuted.author_must_show: How does a json5 value accepted in a UTF8 database restore or replicate into a non-UTF8 database or a newer Unicode version without input errors?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2. The added Unicode-update case is speculative, because new Unicode versions mostly assign new characters, which makes more input valid.

refuted.title: New parameter on makeJsonLexContextCstringLen breaks extension builds
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension that calls makeJsonLexContextCstringLen fails to compile against the new major version. Its maintainer must add version-specific #ifdef code, although the extension has no interest in JSON5.
refuted.argument: 0001 adds a json5 argument to an existing exported constructor, and every in-tree caller is changed to pass false. A separate constructor, or a setter on JsonLexContext, would give the same feature without touching existing callers. The proposal does not explain why it changes the signature instead.
refuted.author_must_show: Why change the signature of makeJsonLexContextCstringLen instead of adding a new constructor or a setter that leaves existing extension callers unchanged?

critic.reasoning: Postgres gives no source compatibility for backend C APIs across major versions, and this constructor's signature has changed before. A compile error is loud and the fix is one argument.

refuted.title: Permanent core json5 type without shown demand or functions
refuted.failure_scenario: Release N ships json5 with casts to json and jsonb, and an implicit json-to-json5 cast. Users create json5 columns, so the type, its OID and its cast rules must stay forever. Later JSON work, such as SQL-standard functions, has to decide each time how json5 behaves, with almost no users to show for it.
refuted.argument: Only the configuration format prototype motivates the type (message #1), and the material does not say whether that proposal still needs it. The type has no functions or operators, so its users get validation plus verbatim storage, which an extension could give once the jsonapi flag exists. The recorded objection in [P1], a niche use that could be an extension, applies to commit 0007. The author offers to drop it (message #1), which leaves the parser work standing.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users, besides the configuration format prototype, need a json5 SQL type in core rather than a parser flag that an extension can use?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1 for the missing demand and of already-exists-1 for the extension route. Those two state each point more concretely.

refuted.title: Two grammars in one shared parser, and the parsers diverge
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch fixes a lexer bug or adds a check on the strict path in jsonapi.c and misses the json5 branches. Tests stay green because FORCE_JSON_PSTACK builds route json5 to the recursive-descent parser, and the incremental parser has no json5 mode at all. The gap appears as a field bug report.
refuted.argument: Commits 0001 to 0006 add json5 branches across the lexer, escapes, numbers and keys of the common parser, and 0005 adds a separate number lexer. The recursive-descent and incremental parsers now accept different languages, so a future change must think about three cases. The area owner commented only in another thread (message #2), and no committer has posted here.
refuted.author_must_show: Has a committer who maintains jsonapi.c agreed to own the json5 branches, and what keeps the strict, json5 and incremental paths from drifting apart?

critic.reasoning: The scenario of a later fix missing the json5 branches is not concrete, and the patch set carries the full json5-tests suite on those branches. The incremental parser stays strict because of the area maintainer's comment, and committer ownership belongs under committability.

refuted.title: Everyone pays libpq size and parser complexity for an optional syntax
refuted.failure_scenario: Every libpq client grows by about 70 KB, and every extension that calls makeJsonLexContextCstringLen must change its call, even though none of them parses JSON5. Later fixes to the shared lexer must be checked against both grammars, while the benefit goes only to json5 users.
refuted.argument: Message #2 states the libpq size cost and offers to drop it, but gives no frontend caller that needs JSON5; parse_manifest and the OAuth code pass false. The new constructor parameter changes the API for all callers. The proposal does not say whether the configuration format proposal still needs this work, so the one concrete consumer may be gone.
refuted.author_must_show: Which backend or frontend caller, other than the json5 type itself, would set the json5 flag, and does the configuration format proposal still depend on it?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2 for the libpq size cost and of already-exists-2 for the missing caller. Its constructor signature point is the one refuted under replication-ondisk-2.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: The json5 type stores validated text verbatim, and that stored form must stay valid across pg_upgrade.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: v2-0007 adds rows to pg_type, pg_proc and pg_cast, including an implicit json to json5 cast.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: makeJsonLexContextCstringLen gets a new json5 parameter and JsonLexContext a new flag.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: json5 is a non-standard type name and input syntax next to the SQL/JSON types.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: Raw non-ASCII keys and whitespace are valid only in UTF8 databases, so a dump can fail to restore elsewhere.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The shared parser in src/common/jsonapi.c carries a second grammar, and libpq grows by about 70 KB.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The patches change the JSON lexer used by all json and jsonb input; message #2 reports about 1% noise.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: An extension could provide the json5 type, and clients can convert JSON5 to JSON today.

questions: Does the configuration format proposal still depend on this work, and if so, on which of the eight commits?
Which in-core caller, backend or frontend, other than the json5 type, would set the json5 flag?
Which users store hand-written JSON5 in Postgres today, and what do they do now instead?
What does a built-in json5 type give users that an extension type using the patched parser and the existing cast-to-json lookup cannot?
If no frontend caller enables json5, can the json5 code and unicode_category stay out of the libpq build?

committability.owner_note: A committer who maintains the common JSON parser (src/common/jsonapi.c) and the json/jsonb types would have to own it; none has posted in this thread.
committability.liability: A permanent built-in type with its OID and casts, an ECMAScript 5.1 grammar in the shared parser, and a Unicode table dependency in libpq, with no end date.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 about 11 weeks after v1 with fuzzing fixes and benchmarks, and moved the entry to the next CommitFest.

not_now.evidence_that_would_change_it: A committed or agreed in-core consumer of the json5 flag, such as the configuration format, or requests from independent users who store JSON5 in Postgres. A statement from a JSON parser maintainer that the flag is wanted for extensions would also help.

priority.reason: Eight patches of about 150 KiB change the shared lexer and add a permanent type, while the thread names one consumer and has no reviewer reply. Splitting the parser flag from the type and tying the flag to a named consumer would give reviewers something smaller to decide.

provisional_note: The effect of the implicit json to json5 cast on function and operator resolution could not be checked without the catalog entries. The level 2 objections on the type-versus-function choice, encoding-dependent validity and libpq size survived but were not evaluated here.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add jsonb_translate(jsonb, from, to)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andrew Dunstan, Pavel Stehule, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds jsonb_translate(jsonb, from, to), and in v2 json_translate, which recursively replaces every value, including array elements, that exactly equals a given string with another string. The author meant it for mapping categorical or enum values deep inside a document, in the style of the Unix tr utility.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrew Dunstan judged blind replacement of every instance of a string, regardless of context, to be a niche use and asked why it could not be an extension. Pavel Stehule suggested using JsonPath to say what to replace, and Peter Eisentraut pointed to json_transform in Oracle and the SQL standard draft, noting that json_transform and json_translate together might confuse users. The thread ends there, and the author later withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Blindly replacing every
instance of a single string regardless of context seems at best a niche
use. Is there any reason not to make this an extension?

precedents_retrieved.title: SQL/JSON: JSON_TABLE
precedents_retrieved.authors: Fedor Sigaev (sigaev), Alexander Korotkov (smagen), Nikita Glukhov (n.glukhov), Oleg Bartunov (oleg)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds the SQL-standard JSON_TABLE function, including the PLAN clause and PLAN DEFAULT clause, on top of the separate SQL/JSON functions patch set. JSON_TABLE turns a JSON document into rows and typed columns selected by jsonpath expressions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying after a rebase in July 2020, and the author did not post a new version within four weeks, so it was returned with feedback. Earlier, Pavel Stehule had marked it ready for committer, after his review objections had been resolved.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Something that has not happened in four weeks, so this is marked
as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Jsonb transform for pl/python
precedents_retrieved.summary: A set of extensions (jsonb_plpythonu, jsonb_plpython2u, jsonb_plpython3u) implementing a CREATE TRANSFORM for jsonb in PL/Python, mapping jsonb objects to dicts, arrays to lists, and numerics to Python Decimal via string conversion, and back. The transform works in both directions so functions can take and return jsonb as native Python values.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The reviewer objected that the third version turned unsupported Python objects such as set() into JSON strings instead of raising an error, asked for tests and errors for complex numbers and ranges, and reported that the tests failed on Python 3. The author sent no revised version after that review, and the commitfest manager returned the patch with feedback because it still needed work and had had no updates for more than a week.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So this still needs more work.. I am marking it as returned with
feedback as there has been no updates for more than 1 week.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql JSON output format
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a JSON output format to psql (\pset format json, psql --json/-J) that renders query results as an array of objects, with a compact layout in normal mode and a one-key-per-line layout in expanded mode. Later versions printed numeric and boolean values without quotes and json values as quoted strings, so that SQL NULL and JSON null could be told apart and the output would round-trip for a planned \gedit feature.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers disagreed on corner-case behavior and no agreement was reached. The open questions were how to tell SQL NULL apart from JSON null, whether json/jsonb values should be embedded as JSON or quoted as strings, and how much round-trip safety to require (numeric scale, float precision, array bounds). The last patch version from January 22 drew several replies but no newer version followed, and Robert Haas marked the entry Returned with Feedback. He suggested settling on one behavior everyone could accept or adding a short list of options.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IMHO, the big problem here is that different people want different
corner-case behaviors and it's not clear what to do about that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Generalized JSON output
precedents_retrieved.summary: Refactor the JSON-producing functions in utils/adt/json.c into a common output layer with overridable callbacks, mirroring the existing parser callback API, so that callers such as logical decoding output plugins can customize output (e.g. quoting numeric and bigint values for JavaScript consumers). As a side effect, the patch unified the inconsistent whitespace styles used by the various JSON output functions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers judged the callback infrastructure too large and invasive for its benefit, and held that the numeric-quoting need could be met in the logical decoding plugin itself, for example by reparsing the JSON, which would also handle json/jsonb values the callbacks would not catch. The consensus, stated by Andrew Dunstan and Heikki Linnakangas, was to fix only the whitespace inconsistency in a much smaller patch without the callback machinery; the author said he needed to rethink the approach.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Let's just fix the whitespace and be done, without all the callback
stuff. That should be a much smaller patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: json_table function PLAN clause
precedents_retrieved.authors: Amit Langote (amitlan), Nikita Glukhov (n.glukhov), Nikita Malakhov (nmalakh)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the SQL-standard PLAN clause to JSON_TABLE, which lets the user choose how NESTED paths are joined to their parent and siblings. It builds on the committed JSON_TABLE code and also corrects some earlier JSON_TABLE tests.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Amit Langote and Alexander Korotkov asked for missing documentation, separation of refactoring from new code, and fixes to IsA() use, deparsing and test coverage. The author answered these in v23 four days before the entry was withdrawn, and no message explains the withdrawal.

precedents_retrieved.title: Optimize JsonbContainerTypeName by reordering type checks
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch reorders the checks in JsonbContainerTypeName() so that the array and object bit checks run before the scalar check. The author argued that this avoids calling JsonbExtractScalar() in most cases and reported about 0.8% higher tps for jsonb_typeof().
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Rowley argued that one function call cannot change the speed of a whole query by a measurable amount. His test called the function 1 million times and found the patch 3.5% slower, and perf top showed JsonbExtractScalar using little CPU time. Andreas Karlsson added that scalars are not clearly less common, so the new order would slow some workloads while it speeds up others.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It'll amount to a few dozen instructions for the function out of several 10s of millions, when you consider the cost of processing the entire query.

precedents_retrieved.title: Removing unused trailing linepointers from heap pages
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch truncates unused line pointers at the end of a heap page's line pointer array, which lowers pd_lower and returns that space for tuple data. Later versions also did this truncation during pruning, beyond the VACUUM-only truncation added in Postgres 14.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Geoghegan asked for concrete evidence before the patch could be committed: a benchmark or test showing a measurable benefit, such as smaller on-disk table size, or at least no regressions. That request went unanswered and the thread stalled, so the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I just want to see
some concrete testing, maybe with pgbench, or with an artificial test
case.

precedents_retrieved.summary:

The reverts the following and makes some associated cleanups:

    commit f79b803dc: Common SQL/JSON clauses

precedents_retrieved.title: Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
Reverted commit(s): Revert to 9.6 treatment of ALTER TYPE enumtype ADD VALUE.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Originally committed as 15bc038f (plus some follow-ups), this was
reverted in 28e07270 due to a problem discovered in parallel
workers.  This new version corrects that problem by sending the
list of uncommitted enum values to parallel workers.

Here follows the original commit message describing the change:

To prevent possibly breaking indexes on enum columns, we must keep
uncommitted enum values from getting stored in tables, unless we
can be sure that any such column is new in the current transaction.

Formerly, we enforced this by disallowing ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE
from being executed at all in a transaction block, unless the target
enum type had been created in the current transaction.  This patch
removes that restriction, and instead insists that an uncommitted enum
value can't be referenced unless it belongs to an enum type created
in the same transaction as the value.  Per discussion, this should be
a bit less onerous.  It does require each function that could possibly
return a new enum value to SQL operations to check this restriction,
but there aren't so many of those that this seems unmaintainable.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent proposed JSON5, relaxed JSON syntax or a new JSON text type. [P1] (jsonb_translate) and [P6] (pluggable JSON output) are in the same area, but their recorded reasons concern a niche value-replacement function and output callback machinery, and neither reason carries over here. Message #2 cites Andrew's comment in another thread about the incremental parser, and v2 drops incremental parser support in response, so no earlier objection is left open. Message #1 links the configuration format proposal as the origin, but the material does not report any objection from it.
Not applicable. The implicit json to json5 cast and its effect on function resolution could not be checked without the catalog entries.

The other persistent changes are the new pg_type, pg_proc and pg_cast rows, storage as verbatim text, and a binary-coercible json to json5 cast. These add no WAL, wire protocol or relation format change, so they raise no concern from this angle.

The proposal adds no privileges, roles or file access, and every existing caller, including the libpq OAuth and manifest code, passes json5=false, so untrusted input does not reach the new grammar there. Parse depth and input size limits are unchanged, so we see no new denial-of-service path without reading the code.
Not applicable; three objections listed. Hot-path cost for strict JSON was measured at about 1% noise (message #2), so I raise no performance objection.
Two objections raised. The JSONC-only first commit also lacks a named in-core consumer, so it is covered by the second objection.
Two objections raised. Both are 'not now, show demand' rather than rejection of the idea.
